messages:
zoe: quick flag 4 PR #5498 (rollouts + retry examples) is blocked on a runtime question. the example in api-client.md shows `client.call(..., retry='auto')` and then an example of a canary rollout, but we don't say which errors are retried by default. need a short authoritative sentence before I merge.

jin: which errors are you showing being retried? link?

zoe: in the diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5498/files see the JS snippet under "canary rollout". it demonstrates a 10% canary then 90% stable, and the snippet uses `retry: 'auto'`. readers will assume network-level retries for 5xx but the runtime has special behavior for idempotency.

emma: CI preview failed when I tested earlier, looks like the new `deployments/rollouts.md` anchor isn't in the nav yet. mkdocs error: ```NavigationError: The 'deployments/rollouts.html' page is not found``` ci-bot gave preview link: https://ci.redwood-inference.dev/preview/5498

ci-bot: preview status: failed  https://ci.redwood-inference.dev/preview/5498 (see logs)

oliver: @jin can you confirm runtime defaults for `retry='auto'`? specifically: are non-idempotent requests retried? what about 429 vs 5xx?

jin: confirmed: `retry='auto'` retries only idempotent-safe errors by default. breakdown: 429 (rate limit) -> client will retry with backoff only if request is idempotent; 5xx (server errors) -> transient 5xx are retried for idempotent requests; timeouts -> retried if idempotent. Non-idempotent endpoints (e.g., stateful modify ops) will NOT be retried unless you pass `force_retry=true` and accept possible duplicate effects. SDKs set idempotency based on method type.

zoe: great, i'll update the docs text to explicitly say that `auto` respects idempotency and mention `force_retry` opt-in for non-idempotent calls. also will add a small example showing how to mark a request idempotent with `Idempotency-Key` header for POSTs.

emma: sounds good. i'll re-run preview after updates. also please add a note about rollout traffic split semantics: we currently route by token hash, not per-session, so a user can hit different variants across requests. readers will expect session-affinity sometimes.

jin: yes, runtime does hash-based routing for rollout percentages. session affinity is not guaranteed unless you enable the `sticky_sessions` flag on Dedicated deployments. worth calling out.

zoe: will add paragraph: "rollout percentages are token-hash based; enable sticky_sessions for session affinity on Dedicated."

docs-bot: reminder  add a CHANGELOG entry and the `docs-next` label. also include a small "runtime-clarifications" note for reviewers.

zoe: added changelog and label, pushing now.

emma: preview re-run started.

ci-bot: preview status: success  https://ci.redwood-inference.dev/preview/5498 (rendered)

emma: content renders, links fixed, examples look OK. i left one micro-nit: the JS example used `retry: 'exponential'` elsewhere; unified to use `retry: 'auto'` here.

jin: LGTM on runtime parts. small FYI: default `max_concurrent_requests` per model instance is 8 unless overridden in Dedicated config; i added a short parenthetical.

oliver: docs review done, grammar tweak, approved. :shipit:

zoe: thanks all  merging to main. i'll watch the docs prod build for 30m and open a revert if anything odd shows up.
